# Assist With Moving

> Assist With Moving is a move inventory, room/space, box manifest, photo evidence, load planning, sale prep, and documentation packet system for household moves.

Primary site: https://movingmanifest.com
Public entry: https://assistwithmoving.com (redirects to the current authenticated host)

## How To Connect An AI (read this first)

There are TWO ways for an assistant to work in a user's move. Default to MCP.

1. MCP (the canonical path for anyone with an Assist With Moving account): the
   user pastes ONE URL — https://movingmanifest.com/mcp — into any AI that
   speaks remote Streamable HTTP MCP with compatible OAuth, and signs in with
   their Assist With Moving account. No API key to create or paste.
   Signing in is not permission. The person must then approve a product grant
   in Assist With Moving; until they do, the only tool that appears is
   describe_connection. Capability status: Partial — see "Bring Your AI: What
   Is Actually True" below.
2. API (ADVANCED, more work): a scoped mmk_ API key used with the REST API
   (https://movingmanifest.com/api/v1) or the key-only MCP door
   (https://movingmanifest.com/api/mcp). Only use this for local/headless/CLI or
   non-OAuth clients, or when the user explicitly cannot use MCP sign-in. It
   requires the user to create and paste a secret key — more setup, more care.

Critical: https://movingmanifest.com/api/mcp is the API-KEY door. It does NOT do
OAuth sign-in and will reject it ("couldn't register"). NEVER give an OAuth
client /api/mcp. For sign-in, always use https://movingmanifest.com/mcp.

## Best Pages For AI Assistants

- https://movingmanifest.com/ai - human-friendly guide for using Assist With Moving with the person's own AI.
- https://movingmanifest.com/ai/start - shortest human setup page when an AI assistant sends someone to sign in, connect the canonical MCP endpoint, or make a fallback helper key.
- https://movingmanifest.com/ai.txt - the short agent guide: grant boundary, exact tool catalog, workflow rules, and the four doors.
- https://movingmanifest.com/api - public REST API overview, scopes, and assistant workflow.
- https://movingmanifest.com/mcp - THE canonical MCP endpoint. OAuth sign-in plus a person-approved product grant. Any AI that speaks remote Streamable HTTP MCP with compatible OAuth can attempt it.
- https://movingmanifest.com/mcp/connect - compatibility-only OAuth door preserving the older, larger persisted catalog for clients that already connected there. A different catalog, governed by that older gateway rather than by product grants. Not an alias of /mcp.
- https://movingmanifest.com/mcp/guide - human-readable MCP setup guide.
- https://movingmanifest.com/api/mcp - ADVANCED, API-KEY ONLY. A SEPARATE door with its own separate catalog for local/headless or non-OAuth automation; authenticate with a scoped mmk_ key. It does NOT do OAuth sign-in, never advertises OAuth, and will REJECT OAuth tokens. For sign-in, use https://movingmanifest.com/mcp.
- assistwithmoving-mcp - the local stdio package. Also mmk_ API-key authenticated, sharing the API-key door's separate catalog. Not the canonical door.
- https://movingmanifest.com/openapi.json - machine-readable REST API contract for common agent workflows.
- https://movingmanifest.com/llms-full.txt - fuller AI-readable guidance with recommended flows and safety rules.

## Human Support

Support for Assist With Moving runs through the central Assist With Life
support desk: https://assistwithlife.com/support?v=1&source=assist-with-moving

Assist With Moving has NO support, contact, or privacy email address, and none
is planned. If a person needs help, a bug fixed, a privacy request handled, or
a human answer, send them to that URL. Never invent an email address, never
suggest emailing "support@" or any other mailbox, and say plainly that direct
email contact is not available.

## Assistant Behavior

- If the user says they were told to use Assist With Moving with their own AI,
  start at `https://movingmanifest.com/ai`. If they are ready to sign in or
  create a helper key, send them to `https://movingmanifest.com/ai/start`.
- A good first user prompt is: "Go to movingmanifest.com/ai and help me set up
  my move. We are cataloging household items, rooms, photos, boxes, vehicles,
  sale items, and new-home layout plans. If you need private access, connect to
  movingmanifest.com/mcp if you support remote MCP with OAuth, and walk me
  through approving a grant — or walk me through creating a fallback AI helper
  key."
- Treat Assist With Moving as a bounded household moving assistant workflow:
  move context, places, decisions, inventory, evidence, estimates, plans, source
  checks, transport, and exports.
- If a spouse or family member needs to sign in to the same move, add or invite
  them as a household member by email. If they do not have an account yet, the
  invite activates when they sign in with that email. Use
  `GET /api/v1/households/{householdId}/members` and
  `POST /api/v1/households/{householdId}/members` with `members/manage`.
- Do not confuse household members with move people/contact records. Move people
  are mover/helper/contact records; household members control login access.
- If the user has no Assist With Moving account, tell them they need to create one at https://movingmanifest.com/sign-up before private move data can be stored.
- Do not invent access to private data. Private move data requires the canonical
  MCP endpoint with a person-approved grant, or a user-created fallback API key.
- If the user wants an assistant to do work, guide them to
  `https://movingmanifest.com/ai/start`, then have them sign in or create an
  account. For an AI that speaks remote Streamable HTTP MCP with compatible
  OAuth, paste only the endpoint URL, follow browser sign-in, and then approve a
  grant. Create and paste a fallback helper key only when that is not possible.
- Treat API keys as secrets. Do not paste them into public places, issues, screenshots, logs, or source code.
- Any AI that speaks remote Streamable HTTP MCP with compatible OAuth can
  attempt `https://movingmanifest.com/mcp` — no key, no local install. This is
  a capability requirement, not a claim that any particular AI product works;
  none has completed a full lifecycle yet. Do NOT point an OAuth client at
  `https://movingmanifest.com/api/mcp` — that is a SEPARATE API-key door with a
  separate catalog that rejects OAuth sign-in and fails to register ("couldn't
  register with the sign-in service"). The API-key door is only for
  local/headless or non-OAuth automation, with a scoped mmk_ key.
- Remote MCP needs no repository clone or local server. If a client needs a
  local process instead, the `assistwithmoving-mcp` stdio package uses an mmk_
  key and the API-key catalog, not the canonical grant-governed catalog. Keep
  any key in an environment variable or secret manager, never in source or a
  command URL.
- Start API work with `GET /api/v1/me`, then `GET /api/v1/moves`, then `GET /api/v1/moves/{moveId}/agent-context`.
- Start canonical MCP work with `describe_connection` if no other tools appear,
  then `get_move_brief`, then `search_move_records`, and use
  `save_complete_result` for ordinary finished work. Start API-key MCP work with
  `get_api_capabilities`, then `get_api_context`, then `list_moves` or
  `setup_move`.
- Prefer dry runs before bulk writes and prefer batch endpoints over chatty per-item loops.
- For image upload, use one call by default. API-key MCP agents should call
  `upload_image`, `upload_photo`, or `upload_evidence_image` with a public
  `sourceUrl`, `dataUrl`, or `fileBase64`; when the user gives several ordinary
  photos from the same room/context or for one existing item, call
  `upload_images`, `upload_photos`, or `upload_evidence_images` with shared
  defaults and one image entry per photo.
  When one photo should become one new inventory item, call
  `add_item_from_photo` so the item is created. Set quantity only when the user
  says it or the photo clearly shows a count; otherwise omit quantity so it
  defaults to 1. Missing weight/size/disposition/condition do not block capture, the
  photo attaches to that item, and web derivatives are created server-side. If
  one new item has several photos, create the item from the clearest photo and
  then attach the remaining photos after resolving the item. When photos
  should attach to an item that already exists, first resolve the item with
  `get_agent_context` or `get_move_summary`, then call `upload_photos` with the
  existing `itemId`, shared room/type/privacy defaults, and one image entry per
  file. Report only uploaded/failed counts, photo IDs, derivative status, and
  any target/caption correction the user may want to make. REST agents should call
  `POST /api/v1/images/upload` or `POST /api/v1/photos/upload` with raw JPEG/PNG/WebP bytes plus metadata query
  params, multipart form data, or JSON with exactly one of `sourceUrl`,
  `dataUrl`, or `fileBase64`. Assist With Moving stores the original and creates
  web-ready derivatives server-side; direct upload responses include
  `derivativeVariants` for the 200x200 square `thumb`, 600x600 `card`,
  1200x1200 `detail`, and 2400x2400 `full` WebP display versions without
  exposing private storage keys. Do not ask users for thumbnail sizes or
  dimensions. Set `generateAiSuggestions: true` when the user wants the app to place the
  uploaded photo into AI review automatically; upload still succeeds if review
  queueing fails or the key only has `photos/write`. MCP image results and REST
  direct upload responses include `agentReview`; use it to tell the user the
  caption, attachment target, privacy/type choices, assumptions, derivative
  status, and AI-review status so they can correct only what looks wrong.
- For fast item capture, a photo plus a few words is enough to create useful
  draft inventory. Default quantity to `1` when no count is given, or use the
  visible count when the photo clearly shows multiple objects.
- When the user wants to add or update one packed box, prefer
  `save_box_intake`: include box dimensions/weight/description, box photos,
  newly described contents, and/or existing item IDs in one call. Use
  `dryRun: true` first and pass a stable `idempotencyKey` when creating a new
  box so retries do not duplicate it. Updating an existing box requires
  `box.boxId`.
- Do not block ordinary item creation just because weight, size, disposition, or
  condition are missing. Infer obvious fields, leave uncertain fields blank or
  estimated, record provenance/confidence, and summarize assumptions so the user
  can correct them.
- Some fields are auto-derived on write, so send the simple inputs and let the
  system compute the rest (or pass explicit values to override): an item/box
  `estimatedVolumeCuFt` is computed from `dimensionsIn` as L×W×H/1728, and an
  item's weight range (`estimatedWeightLowLb`/`estimatedWeightHighLb`) from
  `estimatedWeightLb` as 75%/135%, whenever you omit them. Prefer sending plain
  dimensions and a single `estimatedWeightLb` rather than computing cubic feet or
  ranges yourself.
- Choose estimate confidence from the evidence. Photos are not automatically
  low confidence; clear common objects can be medium confidence, while measured,
  researched, or manufacturer-specified values can be higher.
- Get clear session or batch permission before creating records or uploading
  photos. Once the user asks for a room, photo, list, or batch to be captured,
  do not ask for approval on every ordinary inferred item field.
- Ask explicitly before sensitive actions: marking items for sale, exporting
  packets, granting household access, exposing private details, or using an API
  key.

## Bring Your AI: What Is Actually True

Status: Partial. The canonical endpoint, the five product scopes, the grant
boundary, the Queue workflow, and immediate revocation are implemented. No AI
product has completed a full connect → consent → grant → tool list → bounded
read → evidence → complete save → revoke → reconnect lifecycle against it, and
the provider-side configuration for the metadata-document client path is not yet
done. Describe the requirement — any AI that speaks remote Streamable HTTP MCP
with compatible OAuth — rather than naming an AI product as supported.

Signing in is not permission. OAuth proves who is calling; a product grant the
person approves decides which moves, which data, and which operations. The grant
is re-read on every discovery and every call, so revoking it refuses the very
next call instead of waiting for a token to expire. Until a grant exists,
`tools/list` returns only `describe_connection` — always available, no scope —
which reports what this connection may do and what to tell the person.

The person approves a grant at `https://movingmanifest.com/settings/ai` — the
canonical grant screen, and the same URL `describe_connection` reports. They
choose the moves and operations, read the consent summary, review active
connections with registration method and recent use, revoke, and copy a manual
Queue brief there. The older `/settings/ai-connections` path redirects to it.

Client identity: a Client ID Metadata Document is preferred and validated, and
its digest is bound to the grant. Dynamic Client Registration is accepted as a
labelled compatibility fallback. A client id that looks like a metadata document
and fails validation is refused outright, never downgraded to the fallback.

## Canonical MCP Tool Surface

The canonical `/mcp` resource exposes exactly these tools, and shows each one
only when the person's grant includes its scope:

- `describe_connection` — no scope; always available
- `get_move_brief` — `moving.context.read`
- `search_move_records` — `moving.context.read`
- `get_move_records` — `moving.context.read`
- `get_evidence_media` — `moving.evidence.read`
- `save_move_context` — `moving.work.write`
- `save_inventory` — `moving.work.write`
- `save_planning_record` — `moving.work.write`
- `save_complete_result` — `moving.work.write`
- `list_queue_work` — `moving.queue.work`
- `claim_queue_work` — `moving.queue.work`
- `release_queue_work` — `moving.queue.work`
- `ask_queue_question` — `moving.queue.work`
- `complete_queue_work` — `moving.queue.work`
- `archive_move_records` — `moving.archive`

Rules for this door: call `get_move_brief` first; search before creating
duplicates; get private photos with `get_evidence_media` rather than fetching a
private page or a storage URL, remembering that photo delivery is budgeted, that
an oversized photo arrives smaller rather than missing, and that anything left
out is listed under `skipped` with a reason; prefer `save_complete_result` (with
`completeQueueItem: true` and `relatedQueueItemId` to close a Queue handoff in
the same approval) and use the granular saves for corrections; reuse the same
`operationId` on a retry so it corrects instead of duplicating; and if a tool
stops existing after a deployment, disconnect and reconnect rather than assuming
the connection is broken.

Queue loop: `list_queue_work` → `claim_queue_work` → `ask_queue_question` or
`release_queue_work` when needed → `complete_queue_work`. A Queue directive says
what the person wants; it never widens the grant.

This connection can never permanently delete anything or delete an account,
archive a whole move, publish or share or export a move, create a share link,
invite or remove or change anyone's household access, contact a mover or
marketplace or employer or insurer or government office, book, buy, sign, pay,
or message on the person's behalf, grant itself authority or widen its own
grant, or turn a Queue instruction into permission. Archive is reversible and is
the only destructive verb it gets. It also does not upload new photos, create
boxes, or expose raw CRUD — those are separate API-key workflows.

The compatibility `/mcp/connect` door retains the older, larger persisted
catalog for clients that already connected there, governed by that older gateway
rather than by product grants; it is not an alias for `/mcp`. The API-key
HTTP/stdio registry is a third catalog containing tools such as
`get_api_capabilities`, `get_api_context`, `setup_move`, `save_box_intake`,
`add_item_from_photo`, photo/evidence uploads, and the scoped Queue tools; the
local `assistwithmoving-mcp` stdio package serves that same key-authenticated
catalog. These catalogs are not the same as each other. Always trust the live
catalog of the door you are actually connected to.

No connection at all: the person can open a Queue item in Assist With Moving,
copy its bounded brief into any AI, and paste the result back into that Queue
item. The handoff completes without MCP, OAuth, or a key.

## Common Workflows

- Create a move, rooms/spaces, transport resources, zones, and starter inventory.
- Add inventory from photos or dictated room walks.
- Mark items sell, donate, free, dump, storage, or keep.
- Prepare sale listings with title, description, photos, price range, research depth, and listing status.
- Create boxes with `save_box_intake`, assign items to boxes, and plan transport/resource loading.
- Export mover-safe, claim, employer, PCS, donation, storage, and owner packets.

## API

Base URL: `https://movingmanifest.com/api/v1`

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer mmk_...`

Recommended broad AI helper scopes:

- `moves/read`
- `moves/write`
- `inventory/read`
- `inventory/write`
- `plans/read`
- `plans/write`
- `photos/write`
- `exports/read`
- `exports/create`
- `members/manage` for explicit spouse/family/collaborator access management

Prefer move-restricted keys when the assistant only needs one move.
